::: {.cite-bar .domain-war-powers}
[In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Pub. L. 108-375]{.cite} [118 Stat. 1811]{.cite} [10 U.S.C. 127e]{.cite}
:::

Lets the Secretary of Defense fund foreign forces, irregular forces, groups, or individuals who support or facilitate ongoing U.S. special operations against terrorism. These are surrogate forces working to U.S. objectives, as distinct from partner forces being built up for their own missions.

## Key provisions

- Annual spending cap, set at 100 million dollars.
- Requires the concurrence of the relevant chief of mission.
- Advance notice to the congressional defense committees before a program starts or changes.
- States that it does not itself authorize covert action or the use of force.

## Why it matters

It is a prime example of a Title 10 authority that resembles intelligence work but is overseen by the armed services committees. Programs under it support operations generally conducted under the [2001 AUMF](aumf-2001.qmd), are run by the command created by the [Nunn-Cohen Amendment](nunn-cohen-1986.qmd), and differ in purpose from capacity building under [Chapter 16 of Title 10](seccoop-2016.qmd).

## Current status

In force. It began as the temporary Section 1208 of the FY2005 defense authorization and was made permanent in Title 10 by the FY2017 act.
